IC1: Patient [NOT] not expected to survive more than 4 days
IC2: Patient allergic to a penicillin  [OR]or a carbapenem
IC3: Patient with significant polymicrobial bacteraemia (that is, a Gram positive skin contaminant in one set of blood cultures is not regarded as significant polymicrobial bacteraemia).
IC4: Treatment is not with the intent to cure the infection (that is, palliative care is an exclusion).
IC6: Use of concomitant antimicrobials in the first 4 days after enrolment with known activity against Gram-negative bacilli (excep[NOT] t trimethoprim/sulphamethoxazole may be continued as Pneumocystis prophylaxis).
IC7: Severe acute illness as defined by Pitt bacteraemia score of >4
IC8: Likely source to be from (proven or suspected at the time of randomisation) the central nervous system, e.g. brain abscess, post- [OR]surgical meningitis, shunt [OR] infection (due to concerns over CNS penetration of piperacillin/tazobactam)
